title: Urgent customer briefing structure (personal prep)
body:
Purpose / quick summary:
This is my working scratch for the 1:1 / rapid briefing with the customer execs (scheduled 11/09 09:30 PST). Goal is two-fold: 1) get alignment on visible mitigations and timeline, 2) leave them with a clear runbook and single point of contact while engineering stabilizes the root cause.

Background (one-liners to read before call):
- Customer: BrightForms (enterprise, Dedicated, us-west1 region).
- Incident: increased 5xx rate on text-gen endpoints (model: redwood-v2-13B-fp16-optim) starting 11/07 22:00 PST, intermittent KV cache evictions observed, latency SLO breaches for ~30% of requests.
- Current state: throttles + fallback routing in place to smaller variant; bulk of traffic now served but some degredation persists for long-seq requests; root cause suspected mem fragmentation on dedicated pool nodes.

Desired outcomes for this brief:
- Customer understands exactly what we have done and what we will do next (no surprises).
- Commit to a measurable remediation timeline (T+6h: temporary kernel tweak; T+24h: full pool restart + kernel patch; T+72h: follow-up with post-mortem and regression tests).
- Agree escalation cadence and a single customer liaison (Priya).

Attendees (internal / customer):
- Internal: Anika (CS), Priya (SRE lead), Mateo (infra on-call), Ravi (solutions AE - optional).
- Customer: Sarah (TPM), Omar (platform eng), Lina (ops).

Run of show (20–30m):
- 0:00–2:00 quick intros and roles (confirm who needs updates after call).
- 2:00–6:00 timeline summary: what happened, when, impact metrics (p95 latency, error-rate spike, throughput drop).
- 6:00–12:00 current mitigation steps + immediate mitigations we applied (fallback routing, model variant, temporary throttles).
- 12:00–18:00 plan & timeline for remediation (steps + ownership + risks).
- 18:00–24:00 customer Qs, decision items (e.g., approve immediate pool restart window).
- 24:00–30:00 confirm follow-ups, comm channels, and next check-in time.

Metrics to share (prep: pull latest graphs from Console):
- 5xx rate (last 48h), p95 latency, active connections per node, memory pressure / GPU mem alloc graphs, KV cache hit rate, request size distribution (percent long-context > 4k tokens).
- Quick numbers snapshot to read live: current 5xx = 1.8% (down from 3.6%), p95 = 780ms (target 250ms), cache hit = 62% (baseline 88%).

Communication templates (copy-and-send post-call):
- Internal summary to SRE/infra: "BrightForms incident update: 11/09 09:30 PST call with customer. Current mitigations: fallback to v2-small, throttles at 80% of baseline, kernel mem config tweak applied to 3/6 nodes. Next steps: full pool restart (owner: Mateo) in 6–8 hours if stability not restored. JIRA: JIRA-INC-4021."
- Customer follow-up note (send within 30m): "Thanks for joining — summary here: what we saw, mitigations we applied, next steps + expected ETA, who to contact. We will provide live ETA updates in this thread and follow up with a full post-mortem within 72 hours."
(Include a short template in the email body to paste after the call).

Immediate asks for engineering (quick checklist to ping Mateo / Priya):
- Check kernel mem allocator logs on nodes a-c (Mateo) — link to logs: confluence://cust-telemetry-runbook#brightforms-alloc.
- Validate KV cache eviction pattern and TTLs (Priya).
- Prepare safe restart plan (rolling restart with warm-up steps, Canary tests) and estimated downtime window.
- Run load replay on staging with restored fragmentation pattern to reproduce locally.

Fallback and customer-facing mitigation options (list to offer if they ask for aggressive options):
- Reduce allowed max_seq for customer traffic to 2k tokens (low effort, immediate, degrades longest requests).
- Switch customer routing to result-cached endpoint with higher p99 but lower cost (short-term).
- Provision a dedicated hot spare node and shift traffic (requires approval, expected 1–2 hours to warm).

Decision points we need from customer on call:
- Approve rolling restart in maintenance window (preferred: next 6–10 hours).
- Allow temporary token limit (yes/no).
- Preference for daily sync cadence until RC (daily 09:30 PST or twice-daily?).

My notes-to-self / talking points (short bullets):
- Be explicit about what we DO and DO NOT know. Do not overpromise root cause timing.
- Use customer-oriented language: "we have reduced impact by X, next step will likely remove the root cause but we will validate".
- Offer tight observable commitments: provide 1-hourly checks in the thread until resolved.
- If asked about SLA credits, defer to account team (Ravi) but confirm we'll include mitigation timeline and evidence.

Post-call action grid (to fill during call and send after):
- Action (short): Owner | ETA | Status | Notes (all free-text)
- Example entries to create live: "Pool restart" : Mateo | 2024-11-09T16:00Z | planned | waiting customer ack
- "Kernel patch rollout" : Mateo | 2024-11-10 | planned | patch PR #789 on infra repo
- "Customer comms (daily)" : Anika | daily 09:30 PST | ongoing | send internal + customer short update

Draft post-mortem outline (to be completed by engineering):
- Summary of impact
- Timeline of events (with timestamps)
- Root cause hypothesis + evidence
- Actions taken and rationale
- Post-incident mitigations (short-term and long-term)
